correctness.rationale: For normalized Bargmann–Fock kernels on a regular n-point circle, Gram diagonalization yields lambda_j=n exp(-t) sum_(k>=0)t^(j+kn)/(j+kn)!, exactly n times Poisson residue probability. Independent Poisson increments give strictly positive circular convolution, strictly decreasing max and increasing min of each nonconstant residue law for finite t>0, so κ_n(t) strictly decreases continuously from ∞ to 1 and t_n(C) is unique for C>1. For t=alpha n², Fourier inversion over residue indices, with signed frequency bound exp(-8alpha k²), gives uniform-in-residue approximation to wrapped Gaussian heat kernel H_alpha((j-alpha n²)/n). The phase grid mesh 1/n samples its continuous extrema; Jacobi triple product places them exactly at x=0,1/2, proving theta3/theta4 limiting ratio. Heat-semigroup strict positivity gives unique alpha_C, and bracketing t_n(C)/n² yields alpha_C. Independent Poisson residue calculations at alpha≈0.090693, n=18,40,100 found κ≈2.0253,2.00183,2.00057. Known exact Poisson spectrum explicitly distinguished from the new n² limiting extreme condition theorem.

value.rationale: For regular coherent-state Fock interpolation, the exact sharp n-linear geometric radius needed to maintain any prescribed Gram condition bound is a natural and practically useful threshold. It complements the known fixed-rho*n exponentially ill-conditioned regime by identifying the n²-scale bounded-condition phase and its unique theta constant; not merely restating finite Poisson eigenvalues.

limitations: Fixed C>1, equal-spacing and classical analytic Fock kernel only; no variable C, perturbed circles or non-Gaussian weights.
Same-object literature overlap with coherent-state heat kernels remains a bounded historical-priority risk.
